questions.explanation: Each call spawns two more calls, and the call tree roughly grows by a factor of about 1.618 per level, so the work is exponential. Memoization or bottom-up DP reduces it to O(n) by reusing subproblem results.
questions.question: Naive recursive Fibonacci, where fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2) with no memoization, has which asymptotic running time in n?

questions.explanation: A longest common subsequence such as "BCBA" appears in both strings in order, and no common subsequence of length 5 exists. A standard LCS DP table over prefixes gives this length of 4.
questions.question: What is the length of the longest common subsequence of the strings "ABCBDAB" and "BDCABA"?

questions.correct_answer: BFS finds a path with the fewest edges from the start vertex to every reachable vertex, while DFS does not guarantee this.
questions.explanation: BFS expands vertices in layers using a FIFO queue, so the first time it reaches a vertex it has used the fewest edges. DFS uses a stack or recursion and can reach vertices via long, non-shortest paths.
options: BFS finds a path with the fewest edges from the start vertex to every reachable vertex, while DFS does not guarantee this.
DFS always finds the shortest path first because it goes deepest.
BFS uses a stack, so it explores as deep as possible before backtracking.
Both BFS and DFS always return shortest paths, even on weighted graphs.
questions.question: Which statement about breadth-first search (BFS) and depth-first search (DFS) on an unweighted graph is correct?
